title: Canary SLA Oracle and Benchmark Gate Specification
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Title: Canary SLA Oracle and Benchmark Gate Specification

Summary:
This document defines the design, operational contract, and runbook for the Canary SLA Oracle — a deterministic decision service that evaluates canary releases against a defined set of benchmark gates before permitting progressive rollout. The specification ties release tooling to the benchmarking suite and runtime observability so releases are gated by both fidelity (quality) and operational SLOs (latency, error budget, cost).

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable gate for canary decisions that combines synthetic benchmark signals with live canary telemetry.
- Reduce false positives/negatives by using weighted evidence and time-windowed aggregation.
- Ensure fast feedback for small canaries while remaining robust for larger traffic ramps.
- Emit human-readable verdicts and machine-readable artifacts for automation (ok/reject/conditional).

Scope:
This spec covers: Canary SLA Oracle behaviour, benchmark gate definitions, data ingestion and enrichment, verdict calculation, tie-breaking, and required observability hooks. It does NOT specify UI/console layouts; those are product deliverables.

Definitions:
- Canary: A controlled subset deployment of a new runtime component, kernel, or model variant.
- Benchmark Gate: A single pass/fail criterion computed from benchmark or telemetry data (e.g., P99 <= 80ms).
- Oracle Verdicts: {ok, reject, conditional, inconclusive}.

Architecture overview:
1) Ingests two data streams in parallel: static benchmark results from the perf-suite and live telemetry from the canary shard(s).
2) Normalizes metrics to canonical units (ms, tokens/sec, error-rate) and tags by route/model/tenant.
3) Runs gate evaluators and a weighted aggregator to compute a single verdict.
4) Emits a signed artifact (JSON) with detailed gate evidence, confidence score, and rollback recommendations.

Gate taxonomy and thresholds (default):
| Gate name | Input source | Unit | Default threshold | Failure mode | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| latency_p99_path | live telemetry | ms | <= 120 | reject | path is route-specific P99 over 5m window |
| latency_median_change | perf vs baseline | % | <= +10% | conditional | small regressions allowed with review |
| tail_error_rate | live telemetry | errors/1000 | <= 1.0 | reject | counts 5xx and model-failure errors |
| quality_similarity | perf-suite eval | cosine | >= 0.92 | reject | embedding/response-similarity check against baseline |
| cost_per_token_delta | perf-suite and billing | % | <= +15% | conditional | flags large regressions in unit cost |

Aggregation and weighting:
- Each gate produces an evidence object: {gate, status, measured, threshold, weight, rationale}.
- We compute a score S = sum(weight_i * score_i) / sum(weight_i) where score_i = 1 for pass, 0 for fail, 0.5 for conditional.
- Default weights: latency_p99_path=3, latency_median_change=1.5, tail_error_rate=4, quality_similarity=5, cost_per_token_delta=1.
- Verdict mapping: S >= 0.85 => ok; 0.6 <= S < 0.85 => conditional; S < 0.6 => reject; insufficient/conflicting data => inconclusive.

Time windows and sampling:
- Live telemetry: rolling windows of 1m, 5m, 15m; primary decision window is 5m with 15m as confirmation.
- Perf-suite results: treated as single-snapshot evidence with decay function: weight *= e^{-age/48h}.
- Minimum sample floor: for latency/error gates require >= 500 requests in the 5m window or verdict is marked inconclusive.

Data enrichment and canonicalization:
- Normalize percentiles using the runtime's histogram export (OpenMetrics). Convert to ms and apply route-specific knobs (see section on route sensitivity).
- Enrich with: model_variant_id, kernel_commit, instance_type, region, traffic_mix (proportion of streaming/chat/embedding).

Tie-breaking and human override:
- If aggregation yields inconclusive or conditional, the policy allows a human approver to escalate with justification. The Oracle will surface the top three signals that would flip the verdict if they changed.
- Overrides are auditable: approver id, timestamp, justification, and a TTL for the override (default 1 hour).

Runbook: Canary release flow (operators):
1) Author triggers a canary via the release tool with expected traffic fraction and perf-suite job id.
2) Perf-suite runs pre-release benchmarks (synthetic SLOs) and uploads results to the benchmark-store.
3) Release tool marks canary as active; the Oracle begins ingesting live telemetry automatically.
4) Oracle evaluates gates at T+5m and emits initial verdict artifact to the release tool and logs.
5) If verdict == ok => auto-progress to next stage per release policy.
6) If verdict == conditional => hold, notify on-call and product reviewer with evidence bundle.
7) If verdict == reject => trigger automatic rollback policy and create incident for postmortem.
8) If verdict == inconclusive => extend canary for an additional 10m or require perf-suite re-run with larger synthetic load.

Operational alerts and observability hooks:
- Alert: Oracle failure (ingest/compute) => P1 oncall.
- Alert: inconclusive rate > 10% across canaries in last 24h => investigate metric sparsity or perf-suite health.
- Gauges to expose: current_score, gate_pass_rate, evidence_age_seconds, min_sample_count.
- Dashboards: Canary Health (per-release), Gate Violations (heatmap by route), Evidence Drift (time series of quality_similarity).

Example verdict artifact (machine-readable):
```
{
  "release_id": "r-2026-0104",
  "canary_shard": "canary-eu-7",
  "verdict": "conditional",
  "score": "0.72",
  "evidence": [
    {"gate":"latency_p99_path","status":"pass","measured":"95ms","threshold":"120ms","weight":"3"},
    {"gate":"quality_similarity","status":"fail","measured":"0.88","threshold":"0.92","weight":"5"}
  ],
  "timestamp": "2026-06-10T16:12:03Z",
  "artifact_signature": "sha256:..."
}
```

(That JSON is illustrative; the real artifact must be signed and include schema_version.)

Rollout automation examples (CLI snippets):
- Trigger a canary and attach a perf job:
```
redwoodctl release start --component runtime --sha abcd1234 --canary 0.01 --perf-job perf-2026-06-10-phi
```
- Query Oracle verdict:
```
redwoodctl release verdict --release r-2026-0104 --json
```

Quality and calibration process:
- Monthly calibration: update default thresholds and weights against a held-out corpus of releases from the last 6 months.
- Backfill experiments: re-run perf-suite on historical images and compute oracle false-positive/false-negative rates; aim for < 5% FP at current thresholds.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Oracle service owner: eng-serving-runtime - Release Engineering (primary).
- Benchmarking suite ownership: eng-serving-runtime - Perf & Benchmarking team.
- Oncall escalation: runtime oncall rotation.

Testing and release criteria for Oracle service itself:
- Unit tests for gate evaluators and weight decay logic.
- Integration tests against simulated telemetry with deterministic verdict expectations.
- Synthetic canary first-run in staging must show correct artifact emission and signed artifact verification.

Compatibility notes and known limitations:
- Small-traffic tenants: floor on sample counts will cause frequent inconclusive verdicts; teams should use larger synthetic perf-suite runs for such customers.
- Cross-region canaries: network variance will affect latency gates; the Oracle applies region-aware baselines but teams must review region-specific thresholds.
- Model-aware quality gates assume availability of a reference embedding; new-model onboarding must include a reference dataset.

Migration plan for existing gating mechanisms:
1) Run Oracle in shadow mode for two release cycles and compare with legacy canary decisions.
2) Publish discrepancy report and adjust weights/thresholds.
3) Opt-in small set of services for auto-enforcement for 30 days.

Appendices:
A. Route sensitivity knobs table:
| Route type | sensitivity multiplier | recommended median threshold change tolerance |
| api:chat | 1.2 | 8% |
| api:generation | 1.0 | 10% |
| api:embedding | 0.8 | 6% |

B. Benchmark artifact schema (subset):
- perf_job_id (string)
- model_variant_id (string)
- date (ISO8601)
- metrics {latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, tokens_per_sec, quality_similarity, cost_per_token}
